log.msg: **CAUSES B, C AND D ARE CLOSED, AND THE HEADLINE NUMBER IS ZERO TWICE.** Re-measured the design's own census — top-3 findings over 8 pages × 4 widths, 93 in all: **0 ring the analysis root** (was 16 site-wide, 5 of 42 at 3440) and **0 ring a box covering 60% or more of the viewport** (was 47, and 7 of 7 in the top-3). 18 of the 93 are roll-ups and not one of them points at a page-tall container any more. **37 of 93 target a box fully outside the window — the case that used to draw NOTHING** — and each now draws a 3px bar pinned to the edge it left by, tagged with an arrow and the element's name.

**THE ROLL-UP FIX GREW ONE FIELD AND THE RING'S CAPTION CAME WITH IT.** design.md proposed carrying the exemplar's path as a bare string; measured, that fixed the BOX and left the LABEL wrong — aim() is handed the issue's sel, which on a roll-up is the CONTAINER, so the ring landed on the exemplar and captioned it div.md.flow while the detail line beside it read 'worst is p'. So the exemplar is carried as an ADDRESS AND A NAME, an issue-shaped {path, sel}, which lets highlight.js write 'const at = i.spot ?? i' — a finding is its own address when it has no exemplar. Verified live: that same finding now rings the p and tags it with the p.

**AND THE THREE COPIES OF THE RING CONDITION BECAME ONE FUNCTION, which is a deletion rather than an addition.** report.js, live.js and dev/DevBar/layout.js each carried their own spelling of 'aim this view, but only if the path is non-empty' — three places to teach about the exemplar, and live.js had a keep() helper existing solely to be the else branch. All three now call point($view, root, i), which decides and hands the view straight back when there is nothing honest to ring. ⚠ It collided on the way in: highlight.js already had a private point(el, label) for the hover, now hover(). Two identical names one scope apart is the same class of bug that ratios.under() to inside() was in the calibration pass.

**A REAL BUG THE NEW SELECTION SURFACED: THE READOUT RENDERED TWICE ON EVERY OPEN, and the second render was 200ms after the first.** follow() observed .app, then measure() observed the target — the same element — so ResizeObserver delivered TWO initial observations, each restarting the 200ms settle. Nobody noticed while selection was a 14%-alpha wash on a dark rail; with selection visible it is a finding you click that vanishes half a second later. Measured with a MutationObserver on .dev-layout-out: two renders per open, then none. follow() is deleted, measure() owns every observe(), and a 'fresh' set makes the observer ignore the one delivery that is only a repeat of what the run that observed it just measured. Verified: one render per open, and a selection survives.

**THE SECOND SCREEN IS DELETED, AND WHAT MOVED OUT OF IT IS TWO LINES.** report(data) rendered IN PLACE OF the rail's readout, reached by a button called 'full report' and left only by one called 're-run' — the same report twice, one wiping the other, 20 controls in a 272px column with its url wrapping mid-word. Gone from the rail; report.js is untouched and still serves ext/DesignTool/page.js and audit/page.js, which have page width. Two of its parts moved onto the SELECTED finding — the proposed declaration and 'not a problem'. Two deliberately did not: the before/after mirror clones the element at its own size and needs page width, and the six captioned metric cards are documentation, which belongs on the module's page. The readout already showed the same three numbers in one line.

**SELECTION COST ZERO JAVASCRIPT, which is the part worth recording.** aim() already toggled dt-aimed on the clicked row and already held the ring; the row simply never LOOKED different, because the class was --prim at 14% alpha on a dark rail. DesignTool.css turns that into a 2px border down the inline start, and devbar.css reveals the row's .dev-more off the same class. One click, one class, three signals — border, expansion, held ring — and two of the three are CSS. Clicking a second row moves all three; clicking the same row again collapses and releases, because hold()'s toggle always did. ⚠ display is written in devbar.css rather than as a flex utility class in the JS: the utilities live in @layer util, which beats every rule in the rail's own stylesheet, so display:none written against one would never take.

**CONTROLS, COUNTED RATHER THAN CLAIMED (button/select/a/label inside .dev-bar, at 1920).** The LAYOUT SCREEN — the body below the tabs — now holds exactly **2**: `measure`, and `not a problem` on the selected finding. It held 3 (follow the resize, re-run, full report) and 20 with the full report open. Deleted: `full report` with its screen, and `follow the resize`, which is now always on. Renamed: `re-run` to `measure`, which is the honest name for the one thing that answers staleness. ⚠ RAIL-WIDE the layout tab reads **10 visible** where it read 8, because the four width presets moved INTO the head from the `page` tab — the design specified that as a move and it is: the page tab reads 17 where it read 19, and the presets are now beside the number they promise instead of two screens away from it.

**STATE 4 CLOSED WITH ONE LINE: the page tab reported `size 1920 × 1080` (the WINDOW) while the layout tab reported `root 1648px` (the PAGE), 272px apart, on two screens, neither labelled as which — and the four buttons that SET the page width were on the tab showing the window.** Both are one line in the head now, on every tab: `1648px · 103em`, read off .app's CONTENT box, because the shell reserves the rail as padding-inline-end and its border box is the window at every rail width. `size` and `font` are deleted; `em` rides along because every token on this site is em off the body clamp. ⚠ One trap, and it shipped blank once before I caught it: the observer must watch app.$app.el, NEVER document.querySelector('.app') — width.js runs inside App.render() and the shell does not reach the document until inject(), several awaits later, so the query returns null, there is no retry, and the reading stays empty forever.

**390 IS A BOTTOM SHEET NOW, and the measurement was that the tool covered 70% of what it was measuring.** A 17rem rail at 390 is 272px of a 390px window, and `.app` declines to push at that width (the --rail-floor guard in settings.js), so the page was not squeezed — it was COVERED, and every ring the tool drew landed underneath itself. `inset: auto 0 0 0; height: 45dvh; transform: translateY(100%)` leaves the top 55% of the page visible, `html.dev-open { --devbar: 0px }` goes with it (a preset click clears --rail-floor for the session, so without it the page would be squeezed by a rail no longer beside it), grip.css hides the ew-resize strip at the same threshold, and highlight.js scrolls a held target to `start` rather than `center`. Verified: the held ring settles at y=51 with the sheet starting at y=464 — it clears.

**A RAIL DRAGGED WIDE GETS TWO COLUMNS, in two declarations and no breakpoint.** flex-wrap plus `flex: 1 1 20em; min-width: 0` on the readout's two blocks — the numbers and the findings — is one column in a 17rem rail and two above about 40em of rail. Measured at a 900px rail on a 3440 window: stats at x=2553 w=432, findings at x=2996 w=432, same y. ⚠ min-width: 0 is not optional; the monospace detail lines keep a content-based minimum and will not shrink. At 3440 with the DEFAULT 272px rail it stays one column, and that is the honest answer — the 3168px beside it is the page being measured, and audit/ is this tool's wide-screen surface.

**THE TWO UNCALIBRATED BANDS ARE MARKED, AND THE SENTENCE LIVES ON THE BAND.** `measure` and `contrast` were the top two entries in /framework/'s own `weakest` line — the rail was telling Mike his front page's worst problems were two readings the calibration task proved wrong (188px card captions outvoting the prose; a 125.7px demo clock over a 15px median). Both now carry a `caveat` in taste/ranges.js and render with a dotted --warn underline and that sentence as the title, in the weakest line and in the metrics line alike. ⚠ The rail reads the caveat off the band, never a hard-coded list of band names — a second list in the UI is a truth that stops agreeing the day one of them is fixed. Nothing numeric moved: credit() does not read the field.

**TWO DISPLAY BUGS FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: `gap —×` and `used 71.38%`.** A null metric rendered as a dash with its unit still welded on; a dash takes its unit with it now (one `unit(value, u)` helper). And `width_used` printed two decimals next to `50ch` and `0.38×` — three number formats in one line — so it rounds. The third display bug design.md named, `grade undefined · undefined`, was already fixed by the calibration task an hour before this one started.

**VISION: NOTHING BUILT, ONE RULE WRITTEN DOWN, AND THE PATH AUDITED.** Mike's 'do not recompute on resize!!!' has an enforceable form and it is now in ext/DesignTool/readme.md and at the top of vision.js: **ask() may only ever be reached from a click handler — never from a timer, an observer, or a render.** Audited: ext/Ask is imported by exactly three files (DevBar/ask.js, ext/AITask/compose.js, DesignTool/vision.js), vision.js is the only one in this module, and its ask() is reachable only from run(), which is called only from on('click'). The `looks` column from a committed vision.json is step 12 of design.md's build order, explicitly first to cut, and it is BLOCKED anyway: rubric-v2's verdict is NOT YET because the baseline does not reproduce itself (ICC 0.510), so a vision number placed beside a measured one would inherit the measured one's authority. Not built, on purpose.

**ONE PIECE OF design.md DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: the target's persistent dashed outline.** The design wanted the measured target marked on the page for as long as the layout screen is open. The target is `.app` or `.panel.focus`. For `.app` a dashed line at the viewport's own edge carries no bits — the same argument that cause B is fixed by. For a focused panel it would be genuinely useful, but the mark can only live in one of two wrong places: devbar.css styling `.panel.focus`, a class the rail does not emit and must not import ext/Panel to earn, or a class written onto the measured page, which is the exact thing highlight.js exists to avoid. The honest note for a successor: **a focused Panel carrying no mark outside a workspace is ext/Panel's bug, not the rail's** — panel.css scopes `.panel.focus::after` to `.panel-workspace`. The rail's answer meanwhile is the ⌖ target line, which names it and rings it on hover.

**⚠ THE VERIFICATION THAT MATTERED MOST: NO MEASUREMENT MOVED. 24 of 28 rows byte-identical** (7 urls × 390/1280/1920/3440, comparing counts, every metric, taste score/grade/covered, ignored, and the five leading findings). The four that moved are all `/framework/ai/` — the AI dashboard, whose content THIS TASK edits by logging: text 112935 → 113386, nodes 2773 → 2772, one card added. depth, width_used, pad_em and covered are identical on all four. Same content-drift-on-a-self-measuring-page the calibration task recorded. **tests/ 23/23 at 400, 1280, 1920 AND 3440**, unchanged. **taste/corpus/ 26 agree · 2 disagree · 14 n/a**, identical to the baseline taken before the first edit. 17 pages load with zero console errors, zero failed requests and a rendered .active-page — both audit pages, both library wings, the test corpus, the taste corpus, the widths page, DevBar's own doc pages and this log.

**THE TWO CONTROLS WORK END TO END, verified by driving them rather than by reading them.** `not a problem` renders on the selected finding ONLY when the polish tier allows it — on /framework/ at 1280 that is row 0 (`alignment`) and not rows 1 and 2 (`line-height`, `cramped`), which is `deferrable()` doing its job. Clicking it writes `["/framework/|alignment|span.sidebar-label"]` to localStorage, relabels itself `deferred — measure again` and disables; clicking `measure` then re-runs and the census drops from `0 high · 5 med · 6 low` to `0 high · 4 med · 6 low`. The whole loop — select, read the proposed declaration, wave it through, re-measure — is two clicks on one screen, where it used to be a screen swap and a button called `re-run` that was also the way back.

assign.outcome:
**One screen, two controls, and no ring that lies.** The `layout` tab is a single readout again: DesignTool's full report is deleted FROM THE RAIL (it is a page component and still serves the two pages with room for it), and the two things it had that the rail wanted — the proposed declaration and `not a problem` — moved onto the SELECTED finding. **The selection is the expansion, and it cost zero JavaScript**: `aim()` already toggled `dt-aimed` and already held the ring, so a 2px border in DesignTool.css and one `display` rule in devbar.css turn one click into three agreeing signals. The layout screen now holds exactly **2** controls (`measure`, and `not a problem` when the tier allows it), down from 3 and from 20 with the full report open; `follow the resize` is deleted and always on, `re-run` is renamed `measure` because the readout is a snapshot and that is the honest name. The four width presets moved into the **head**, beside the number they promise (`1648px · 103em`) — they used to set the page width from a tab that reported the window, 272px and one click away.

**Highlight causes B, C and D are closed, measured: 0 of 93 leading findings ring the analysis root (was 16 site-wide), 0 ring a box covering ≥60% of the viewport (was 47, and 7 of 7 in any top-3), and 37 that used to draw NOTHING now draw an edge bar tagged `↑`/`↓`.** A roll-up carries the exemplar as `{ path, sel }` so the ring lands on the box that broke AND is captioned with it; three duplicated "aim, but only if…" conditionals collapsed into one `point($view, root, i)`. **390 is a bottom sheet** — a 17rem rail there covered 70% of what it was measuring — and a rail dragged wide gets two columns in two declarations. Two knowingly-uncalibrated bands (`measure`, `contrast`) wear a dotted underline carrying the reason, read off the band in `taste/ranges.js` rather than a list in the UI. Vision: nothing built, one rule written down and audited — **`ask()` may only ever be reached from a click handler**.

⚠ **No measurement moved**: 24 of 28 rows byte-identical, the four that changed all `/framework/ai/`, whose content this task's own log edits. `tests/` **23/23 at 400, 1280, 1920 and 3440**; `taste/corpus/` **26/2/14**, identical to the baseline taken before the first edit; 17 pages load with zero console errors. Two bugs found on the way: the readout **rendered twice on every open** (two initial `ResizeObserver` deliveries) and threw away any selection made in between, and `width.js` shipped blank once because `document.querySelector(".app")` is null inside `App.render()`.
